source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
Downy mildew (ជំងឺទឹកនោលស្លឹក, literally 'leaf water-soaking disease') is a fungal disease of watermelon leaves. It shows up as discoloration/yellowing patches that spread outward across the leaf, and it is worsened by humid, rainy conditions; the disease is illustrated with sample photos of affected leaves in the source.

Spread and risk factors noted include wind and splashing water carrying spores between plants, and the disease becoming more severe in wet weather or where humidity stays high in the field.

Recommended prevention and control measures: pick off and remove leaves showing disease symptoms, collecting them in a basket and disposing of them away from the field rather than leaving them on the ground; keep the field and surroundings free of weeds and volunteer/host plants that can harbor the fungus; and apply fungicide, such as Metalaxyl combined with Mancozeb, or Metalaxyl combined with Fosetyl-Al, especially during humid periods when disease pressure is high.
